relationships.title: Nvidia common stake in Intel
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia paid {funded} for {counterparty} stock tied to a chip collaboration, and its later holdings reports show a smaller stake within a year.
relationships.definition: Nvidia bought 214,776,632 newly issued Intel common shares at $23.28 each for $5.0 billion in cash under a securities purchase agreement signed on 15 September 2025. The sale closed on 26 December 2025 after the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period. The stake came with a collaboration under which Intel builds Nvidia-custom x86 CPUs and x86 SOCs with Nvidia RTX GPU chiplets. Nvidia's 13F shows 161,082,488 shares at 30 September 2026.

committed_total.note: Securities purchase agreement of 2025-09-15; listed in Nvidia's investment commitments at 2025-10-26 subject to regulatory approval.

funded.note: 214,776,632 shares at $23.28 in cash, closed 2025-12-26. Cost of the shares sold later is not disclosed.

contingent_max.note: Plain common equity; no contingent term found.

market_value.note: 13F reported value of 161,082,488 shares at 2026-09-30, filed 2026-11-16, after a reduction from 214,776,632 shares.

holding.note: 214,776,632 shares at 2025-12-31 and 2026-06-30; 161,082,488 at 2026-09-30, a reduction of 53,694,144 shares (analysis). No source states the sale price, date or reason. Percent of class not computed. shares_acquired: 214,776,632 shares bought for the funded amount (Intel 8-K of 2025-12-29, ev_60005).

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia's release (2025-09-18) says it will invest $5 billion at $23.28 per share subject to regulatory approvals; its Q3 FY2026 10-Q lists $5 billion in Intel within investment commitments subject to regulatory approval; its FY2026 10-K reports gains on the Intel stock; its 13F reports 214,776,632 shares at 2025-12-31 and 161,082,488 at 2026-09-30.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: Intel's 8-K (2025-09-18) reports the agreement of 2025-09-15 for 214,776,632 shares at $23.28 for $5.0 billion, subject to HSR, with no governance or information rights; its 8-K (2025-12-29) reports closing on 2025-12-26; its 10-K and Q3 2026 10-Q repeat the terms (215 million shares, rounded).

differences.counterparty_value: Intel reports only the 214,776,632 shares issued; no disclosure of Nvidia sales found
differences.note: Nvidia's Q3 FY2027 cash flow shows $2,253M of proceeds from equity sales without naming issuers (ev_60113).

credit.wwr_reason: Equity loss is capped at cost and does not grow if Intel weakens; Intel's value and the joint products both depend on data center and AI demand, so the stake moves with the AI cycle.
credit.collateral: None. Common stock, last in line behind $50.1 billion of Intel debt.
credit.tenor: Open ended; no lock-up or standstill found in Intel's filings.
credit.notes: The agreement gives Nvidia no governance or information rights (ev_60004). Co-investors in the same period: SoftBank at $23.00 per share and the US government.

first_order.trigger: Intel misses its foundry and joint product milestones
first_order.mechanism: The joint NVLink products slip and Intel's share price falls
first_order.text: If Intel's custom data center and PC products with Nvidia NVLink are late, Nvidia loses value on its remaining Intel shares and the joint products slip.

first_order.trigger: Nvidia continues to sell Intel shares
first_order.mechanism: Nvidia realizes gains and reduces its exposure to Intel
first_order.text: Nvidia cut its Intel holding by a quarter within a year of closing, so its exposure to Intel is falling while the product collaboration continues.

second_order.trigger: Nvidia reduces or exits its Intel stake
second_order.mechanism: Intel's other strategic holders bought on their own terms, so the effect of an Nvidia exit on them is not shown
second_order.text: SoftBank bought Intel shares at $23.00 and the US government took Intel shares and warrants in the same period as Nvidia, and no source says Nvidia's purchase set their terms.

second_order.trigger: Intel's foundry business is sold or spun off below 51% ownership
second_order.mechanism: The US government warrant for 241 million shares at $20 becomes exercisable and dilutes holders
second_order.text: If Intel ceases to own at least half of its foundry, the government warrant dilutes Intel holders, Nvidia included.

depth2_links.description: Bought 87 million Intel shares at $23.00 for $2.0 billion under an agreement of 18 August 2025, closed 26 September 2025.

Received 275 million Intel shares, 159 million escrowed shares released at $20 per share as Secure Enclave funds arrive, and a warrant for up to 241 million shares at $20 exercisable if Intel owns less than 51% of its foundry.

relationships.notes: Seed C1 confirmed: $23.28 per share quoted from Intel's 8-K (ev_60002, ev_60007) and Nvidia's release (ev_30034). Analysis: at the 13F value, the remaining 161,082,488 shares were worth about $120 each at 2026-09-30.

relationships.title: Nvidia multiyear agreements with Amkor, including prepayments
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia's agreements with {counterparty} total {headline} including prepayments for packaging capacity, on terms that neither company has stated.
relationships.definition: Nvidia says it supports Amkor's expansion through multiyear agreements announced in July and October 2026, totaling nearly $3 billion and including prepayments. Amkor's 10-Qs report two advance payment agreements with an unnamed customer in the same months; that this customer is Nvidia is analysis. Some advances are backed by standby letters of credit issued by Amkor.

headline.note: Nvidia says the agreements total nearly $3 billion and include prepayments (ev_30065); the figure is slightly below $3 billion and covers all the agreements, not only prepayments. Dated to the Nvidia statement of 2026-11-17 because the July and October 2026 agreements are not separately valued by Nvidia.

committed_total.note: Unknown: Amkor's advance payment agreements do not name the customer, so no committed amount is attributed to Nvidia. See notes (analysis).

funded.note: Advances under both agreements are expected in 2027.

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia's release (2026-11-17) says multiyear agreements announced in July and October 2026 total nearly $3 billion and include prepayments.
reconciliation.counterparty_side: Amkor's June and September 2026 10-Qs report advance payment agreements signed in July 2026 (about $1.5 billion in 2027) and October 2026 (about $1.3 billion in 2027) with an unnamed customer, plus $200 million of standby letters of credit for advances received.

differences.nvidia_value: nearly $3 billion of agreements including prepayments
differences.counterparty_value: about $1.5 billion plus about $1.3 billion of advances, customer not named

credit.wwr_reason: The advances are credited against packaging work for Nvidia; if AI demand falls, Nvidia orders less, credits slow and the exposure lasts longer without growing.
credit.collateral: Amkor issues standby letters of credit for some customer advances ($200 million outstanding at 2026-09-30); whether any cover Nvidia's advances is not stated.
credit.tenor: Advances expected in 2027; repayment period not stated.
credit.notes: Amkor IR releases on ir.amkor.com could not be fetched (HTTP 403).

first_order.trigger: Amkor's Arizona or Korea capacity is delayed
first_order.mechanism: Nvidia's prepayments are not worked off on schedule
first_order.text: If Amkor's new packaging lines are late, Nvidia's advances to Amkor are worked off later and its packaging supply tightens; Amkor backs some customer advances with standby letters of credit but does not name the customer.

second_order.trigger: Amkor relies on customer advances to fund capex
second_order.mechanism: Amkor's capacity build is partly funded by customer advances from an unnamed customer
second_order.text: Nvidia says its Amkor agreements include prepayments to scale capacity; Amkor does not name the customer, so how much of its expansion Nvidia funds is not disclosed.

relationships.notes: Analysis: Amkor's 10-Qs report advance payment agreements with an unnamed customer signed in July 2026, under which Amkor expects about $1.5 billion in 2027 (ev_60111), and in October 2026, about $1.3 billion in 2027 (ev_60105). The months match the agreements Nvidia announced (ev_30065), which suggests the customer is Nvidia, but Amkor does not name it, so the sum of about $2.8 billion is not entered as committed_total until a source names Nvidia.

relationships.title: Nvidia capacity reservation advance to KYEC
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia says it is advancing {headline} to {counterparty} for test capacity not yet built, so the money is at risk until production starts.
relationships.definition: Nvidia is providing a capacity reservation advance to King Yuan Electronics to support new US testing facilities. The advance reserves test capacity for Nvidia; high-volume production is targeted for April 2027 according to Nvidia. Terms of repayment or crediting are not stated.

committed_total.note: Described by Nvidia as its advance; definitive per the release, not confirmed by KYEC.

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia's release (2026-10-21) says its $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance to KYEC will support new US testing facilities.

credit.wwr_reason: The advance to KYEC is worked off through purchases for Nvidia; if AI demand falls, purchases slow and the exposure lasts longer without growing.
credit.notes: KYEC is not an SEC registrant; kyec.com.tw not searched successfully.

first_order.mechanism: Nvidia's advance is not worked off and test capacity is short
first_order.text: Nvidia's $1.1 billion advance pays for new KYEC testing facilities and equipment in the US, with high-volume production targeted for April 2027, so until then it is not backed by output.

second_order.trigger: KYEC's US sites serve Nvidia's US manufacturing plans
second_order.mechanism: A KYEC delay holds back other US packaging and test steps

relationships.title: Nvidia capacity reservation advance to IBIDEN
relationships.insight_template: Nvidia funds substrate capacity at {counterparty} with an advance of {committed_total}, so a substrate shortfall would hit both its supply and its money.
relationships.definition: Nvidia is providing a multibillion-dollar capacity reservation advance to support IBIDEN's Ono Plant, which makes IC package substrates. Nvidia says the agreement was signed and announced earlier in 2026 by IBIDEN. No amount, term or crediting mechanism is stated.

reconciliation.nvidia_side: Nvidia's release (2026-10-21) says it is providing a multibillion-dollar capacity reservation advance for IBIDEN's Ono Plant.

credit.wwr_reason: The advance to IBIDEN is worked off through purchases for Nvidia; if AI demand falls, purchases slow and the exposure lasts longer without growing.
credit.notes: IBIDEN's capital investment notice (ibiden.com PDF) was fetched but its text could not be extracted; a search snippet says customers bear investment costs partly as advance payments, without naming Nvidia.

first_order.trigger: IBIDEN's Ono Plant ramps slower than planned

first_order.text: Nvidia describes its IBIDEN advance only as multibillion dollar; it funds a tripling of the Ono Plant with new capacity from early 2028, so the amount at risk until then cannot be sized.

second_order.trigger: IBIDEN substrates are used by packaging partners
second_order.mechanism: A shortfall at IBIDEN constrains packaging output at Nvidia's assemblers
second_order.text: A substrate shortfall at IBIDEN would idle packaging lines that Nvidia also prepaid at Amkor and SPIL (analysis).

relationships.notes: IBIDEN's capital investment notice (ibiden.com PDF) was fetched but its text could not be extracted; a search snippet says customers bear investment costs partly as advance payments, without naming Nvidia.

second_order.text: Nvidia now funds both SPIL and Amkor packaging capacity, so a demand fall would leave it with prepaid capacity at two assemblers at once.
